title: Lower-shriek existence from a covering of representable evaluations
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, meaning an adjoint pair $f^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ and $f_*:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ with $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $f^{-1}$ preserving finite limits. Suppose $E$ is a set of objects of $\mathcal D$ such that every object of $\mathcal D$ has a covering by objects of $E$, and for every $V\in E$ there is a sheaf $G_V$ on $\mathcal C$ with bijections $(f^{-1}F)(V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)}(G_V,F)$ natural in sheaves $F$ on $\mathcal C$. Then there exists a functor $f_!:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ with bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)}(f_!G,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)}(G,f^{-1}F)$ natural in $G\in\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ and $F\in\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Thus $f_!\dashv f^{-1}$.

proof.text: Write $R=f^{-1}$. On either site the sheafification existence theorem and its universal property provide $h_V^\#$. The presheaf Yoneda bijection followed by sheafification adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(h_V^\#,K)\cong K(V)$, natural in $K$. Thus the hypothesis gives bijections $\alpha_{V,F}:\operatorname{Hom}(G_V,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_V^\#,RF)$. Put $i_V=\alpha_{V,G_V}(\mathrm{id})$. Naturality in $F$, applied to $u:G_V\to F$, says exactly $\alpha_{V,F}(u)=R(u)i_V$.

The coproducts and coequalizers needed below exist: form a presheaf coproduct by disjoint union at each object, and a presheaf coequalizer by the quotient of the target values by the equivalence relation generated by the two images. Restrictions act on summands and equivalence classes, respectively, and their functor laws follow from those of the original presheaves. These constructions have their universal properties objectwise. Sheafify them; maps to any sheaf factor uniquely through sheafification, so the resulting sheaves have the same coproduct and coequalizer universal properties in the sheaf category. All indexing families are sets, since the sites, $E$, and each sheaf value are small in a fixed universe.

source.place: Tag 00WI, lemma-colimit-sheaves, applied only to coproducts and coequalizers

proof.text: For each set-indexed family $A=(V_j)_{j\in J}$ in $E$, put $P_A=\coprod_jh_{V_j}^\#$ and $L_A=\coprod_jG_{V_j}$. Define $i_A:P_A\to RL_A$ on the $j$th summand as $R(\iota_j)i_{V_j}$. Maps out of a coproduct are families of maps, so the product of the bijections in step 1 yields $\alpha_{A,F}:\operatorname{Hom}(L_A,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P_A,RF)$, with $\alpha_{A,F}(u)=R(u)i_A$. This also covers $J=\varnothing$; the product of empty families is a singleton.

For any morphism $a:P_A\to P_B$ of sheaves (not merely one induced by maps in the site), define $L(a)$ to be the unique map $L_A\to L_B$ with $R(L(a))i_A=i_Ba$, using $\alpha_{A,L_B}$. The identity satisfies this equation. If $b:P_B\to P_C$, then $R(L(b)L(a))i_A=R(L(b))i_Ba=i_Cba$, proving $L(ba)=L(b)L(a)$ by uniqueness. For $u:L_B\to F$ we obtain $\alpha_{A,F}(uL(a))=R(u)i_Ba=\alpha_{B,F}(u)a$. This verifies compatibility for arbitrary arrows between the coproducts, including the two relation maps below.

source.place: Tag 09YX, first two paragraphs, characterization of the induced functor

proof.text: Apply the covering-representable presentation lemma to the small site $\mathcal D$, its covering subset $E$, and an arbitrary sheaf $H$: choose $P_A\rightrightarrows P_B\xrightarrow{q}H$ (with parallel arrows $a,b$) a coequalizer. Define $L_H$ to be the coequalizer of $L(a),L(b):L_A\to L_B$ on $\mathcal C$, with quotient map $\ell:L_B\to L_H$. Only the covering hypothesis is needed for the presentation; no subcanonical topology is assumed.

For a sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal C$, a map $u:L_H\to F$ corresponds uniquely to $v=u\ell:L_B\to F$ satisfying $vL(a)=vL(b)$. By step 4 the bijection $\alpha_{B,F}$ carries this condition exactly to $\alpha_{B,F}(v)a=\alpha_{B,F}(v)b$. The coequalizer property of $q$ identifies such maps with maps $H\to RF$. Denote the resulting bijection by $\beta_{H,F}$. For $t:F\to F\prime$, step 3 gives $\alpha_{B,F\prime}(tv)=R(t)\alpha_{B,F}(v)$. Hence the maps $\beta_{H,F\prime}(tu)$ and $R(t)\beta_{H,F}(u)$ have equal composites with $q$, and coequalizer uniqueness makes them equal. Thus $\beta$ is natural in $F$, as needed in the displayed equalizer calculation in the source.

Put $i_H=\beta_{H,L_H}(\mathrm{id})$; naturality in $F$ gives $\beta_{H,F}(u)=R(u)i_H$. For $c:H\to H\prime$, define $L(c)$ as the unique map satisfying $R(L(c))i_H=i_{H\prime}c$. For the identity, $R(\mathrm{id}_{L_H})i_H=i_H\mathrm{id}_H$, so uniqueness gives $L(\mathrm{id}_H)=\mathrm{id}_{L_H}$. For $d:H\prime\to H\prime\prime$, the equation $R(L(d)L(c))i_H=R(L(d))i_{H\prime}c=i_{H\prime\prime}dc$ gives $L(dc)=L(d)L(c)$ by uniqueness. Also $\beta_{H,F}(uL(c))=\beta_{H\prime,F}(u)c$, proving naturality in $H$. Consequently $H\mapsto L_H$ and $c\mapsto L(c)$ give $f_!$ and the required adjunction. The construction uses chosen set-indexed presentations for each sheaf; uniqueness through these representing bijections also identifies any alternative choice by a unique compatible isomorphism.
